formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement; the strongest of those checks drives the committed record itself from a real proposal, PreAccept round and commit broadcast before the recovery runs. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal. The applied-state consequence of that divergence is confirmed on the same driven history: the direct checks for claim C3-applied-effect-follows-committed-vector show that the recovering replica applies nothing for the instance's key while the replicas holding the real committed vector apply it, so the disagreement between committed vectors also reaches the state machines (artifacts f1d4a9f06e81464aa803ee7809e4e5c6 and 52a176deb66c4588a59d71f8afeb13ab).

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict for every command pair and performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false; the direct check for claim C12-transitive-skip-executes-commuting-command confirmed in scope that with the flag enabled a committed instance whose command commutes with its uncommitted dependency is still not executed, so the documented transitive-conflict skipping is inert and the launcher's false is the only reason the default deployment is unaffected (S45-transconf-block, S46-transconf-doc, S47-run-transconf).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).

the command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven; the three direct checks for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed in scope that a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 bytes with 4477 consumed, that the command following such a value in the same buffer decodes to garbage (op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value), and that decoding a real PreAccept carrying such a value panics with makeslice: len out of range, which the receiver's reader has no recover for. The default configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary. An exploration that drove the real peer reader (execution 5b9267ea51d742f9a6fdcfb7a6594990) observed its reaction to a displaced stream: with the verbose logger the launcher passes, the reader prints an unknown-message-type error and the process exits non-zero; with a non-verbose logger the loop ends silently and the peer is marked not alive. That observation is construction knowledge from an exploration rather than reviewed evidence (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size, S22-replica-listener, S48-logger-fatal).
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.
